prose: A Wccftech Q&A with Nvidia's Vera CPU team argues that agentic AI is reversing a decade of CPU design priorities. The chiplet era - filling packages with as many cores as possible - sacrificed single-threaded performance and IPC, because chiplets leave no space to design for per-core performance and force cores to cross IO boundaries. Agent workloads invert the requirements: an agent runs sequential control logic on the CPU between reasoning steps, and the goal is to finish that sequential work fast and get back to the GPU, keeping the expensive accelerators highly utilized. Nvidia's answer in Vera is a single monolithic compute die where all cores talk to each other without crossing IO boundaries or incurring that latency - a deliberate move back to per-core performance over core counts.
highlights: Nvidia's Vera team: agentic AI is forcing CPU design back to single-threaded performance
Chiplet designs traded per-core performance and IPC for core counts
Agents run sequential control logic on CPU between GPU reasoning steps
Goal: finish CPU work fast and return to the GPU, keeping expensive accelerators utilized
Vera uses a single monolithic compute die; cores communicate without crossing IO boundaries
